newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK export credit insurance up 15.9 pct Apr-Dec '96.
newsitem.headline: HK export credit insurance up 15.9 pct Apr-Dec '96.

text.p: The Hong Kong Export Credit Insurance Corp said in a statement on Thursday total business insured rose 15.9 percent to HK$15.49 billion in the first three quarters of the current financial year ending March 31, 1997.

"While the growth suggests that the economy of our major export markets has been picking up, rising awareness among exporters of the importance of credit insurance may be another underlying factor accounting for the surge of our business," the government-owned entity's general manager, K.K. Cheung, said in the statement.
The United States constituted the largest insured market, accounting for 33 percent of total insured business.
Britain remained the second largest market, making up 17 percent of total insured business, while Germany came third with a 11 percent contribution, the said.
Textiles and garments were the largest category of insured products, contributing HK$4.49 billion or 29 percent of total insured business.
Claims paid amounted to HK$55.66 million, 72 percent higher year on year.
Insolvency accounted for 26 percent of the total claims paid. Default accounted for 66 percent of claims or HK$36.79 million, representing a 197 percent year-on-year rise.
The increase in claims payment was due to the rising number of cases involving buyers in the U.S., Germany and Italy, the statement said.
A record claims payment of HK$13 million arising from default of a Chinese buyer also added to the rise in claims payment, it added.
